perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s perspective, the information available to him is:

- He is managing a project whose team he perceives as unmotivated and underperforming, which leaves him frustrated, anxious, and worried.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a friend/advisor he can consult; they meet at a coffee shop.
- In their first conversation, Harold tells Arthur that his project team seems completely unmotivated and is affecting progress. Arthur advises him to understand what drives each team member individually and to have one-on-one conversations. Harold admits he had focused mainly on goals and deadlines, agrees to try Arthur’s suggestion, and feels more hopeful afterward.
- Harold then tells his team he wants one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them. Team Member 1 says that could be helpful; Team Member 2 says they are open to it. Harold says he will schedule individual times and wants the project to succeed together.
- Later, Harold observes that the team still is not responding well. He tells Arthur he tried the suggestions but the team still isn’t responding, and he is worried about the project’s future. Arthur suggests there may be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors. Harold agrees to set up another round of meetings.
- In those meetings, Team Member 1 tells Harold there is tension between a few team members affecting work. Team Member 2 tells Harold they feel overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard. Harold says he will look into resolving conflicts and consider redistributing tasks, and that their well-being matters.
- Harold then tells the team he has heard their concerns and will create regular feedback sessions and team-building activities for a more supportive environment. Team Member 1 and Team Member 2 respond positively. Harold says he is glad and emphasizes shared success and the importance of their input and well-being.

Harold has no direct access to private thoughts, hidden motivations, or narrator-only facts about Arthur or the team beyond what was said or observed in these interactions.
